items.title: One taxonomy for everything: areas say where, kinds say what
items.question: The first fixtures made "project" mean anything with a view, so an internship application got a Project view, opened in the Project window that follows tmux, and showed blank under another project's name. The first fix, a kind called project, left the word doing two jobs (a part of life and a shape of thing), so 3YP looked as if it belonged in three places, and the labelling is key to the backend logic.
items.chose: Every item carries two independent labels from one global taxonomy: an area (Studies, Projects, Careers or Personal: which part of your life) and a kind (what shape of thing it is, which decides its machinery and its screen). The registry holds three kinds, repo, course and application, and the Project window shows repos only.
items.why: Splitting where from what means a kind never implies an area and an area never implies a kind, so nothing has to sit in two places. A thing that seems to be two kinds is two linked things: B3 Group Design Project is a course and 3YP is the repo that does its work, linked by its course. A due date is an attribute that a task, an application's stage or a course milestone can carry, hard or soft, rather than a kind of its own. The taxonomy lives in the shared root in this repository and is served by the one HTTP service, so every app reads the same one, and which app stores a thing (kairos keeps tasks, keryx keeps mail) plays no part in how it is labelled. The Project window then needs no special cases: it only resolves a tmux session to a repo, whatever the repo's area.
over: "Project" as anything with a view, as the first fixtures had it: an application opened in the Project window, which follows tmux, and showed blank under another project's name
A kind called project alongside the area called Projects: the word did two jobs, area and kind, so 3YP looked as if it belonged in Studies, Projects and course at once
Letting one thing be two kinds (3YP as both course and repo): replaced by two linked things, the course and the repo that does its work
A deadline as its own kind of object, as kairos has it: a due date is an attribute of whatever it belongs to
Labelling a thing by the app that stores it: storage is a detail and plays no part in how something is labelled
assumes: Every item has exactly one area; if things often need two areas at once, areas become tags instead
Labelling tracks Studies by default does not misfile them, although prep plans in Careers use them; if it misfiles them in search or the weekly review, tracks get no area and inherit their goal's
costs: kairos changes: its task types become sheet, coursework, admin and chore, and its separate deadline object becomes a due date on whatever it belongs to
New screens to build: an Application screen, and later a course view with Canvas
Tracks sit in Studies by default even when a Careers prep plan uses them
evidence: Under the first fixtures an application opened in the Project window and showed blank under another project's name
Every area by every kind was laid out against real examples, from B15 sheet 3 and 3YP to Jump, G-Research, Millennium and Futsal, to check each thing has one place

you.text: Do applications and my CV really count as projects ... they are internship applications and my CV, they do not feel like projects
Need to sort how we treat this properly once and for all, as this is a slightly messy taxonomy issue that I would like to sort as it is key for the backend logic
3YP seems to belong in both studies and project, (and course) ... this still feels really clunky ... include, with examples EVERYTHING and where it gets labelled
A studies section could be good actually ... the projects section on the home page could be personal projects, and then 3YP could go in the studies section

affects: The shared contract: project kinds become repo, course and application, a repo links to its course, and the Project view gains questions from the dossier and a due list
Home: a section per area, with personal projects under Projects, careers and studies side by side, and Personal shown through the calendar and chores
The Project window, which follows the project window's tmux session and shows repos only
kairos task types and deadlines, a change raised in Slice 0
The Application screen in Slice 1, and the course view and Canvas in Slice 7
Every app, which reads the same taxonomy and registry through the one HTTP service

items.title: The data directory is data/, not vault/
items.question: The directory in the checkout holding the database, the raw store, the drop zone, his notes, backups, caches, logs and the Obsidian export was called vault/, which reads as an Obsidian vault, and one sits inside it. Renaming it was not just a rename, because paths under it are stored as identity: they are how an edited note is found and replaced, and they key the agent tables.
items.chose: Rename vault/ to data/ everywhere (config defaults, the example config, code, tests, units, the outbox, CLAUDE.md), with migration 0037 rewriting the stored paths and no compatibility symlink.
items.why: The old name invited confusion with Obsidian's vault. library/ was the other candidate, but the plan already uses "the library" for the frozen engine and its sources, and this directory also holds his notes, backups and caches, so data/ is the accurate name. Because stored paths are identity, renaming the directory alone would have made every edited note arrive as a second document, silently, so the stored paths are migrated in the same change. On the server the directory moves once, inside the server sync script, under the ingest lock, and its config is rewritten there.
over: Keep vault/: the name reads as an Obsidian vault, and one sits inside it
library/: the plan uses "the library" for the frozen engine and its sources, and this directory also holds his notes, backups and caches
Rename the directory without migrating stored paths: every edited note would have arrived as a second document, silently
assumes: The directory stays one thing; if it ever splits into a library store and his notes, the parts get named then
costs: Long-running MCP sessions started before the deploy hold the old config and cannot open the database until they restart
Corpus text that mentions vault/ still says so, because derived layers do not edit what a document said
Model prompts that call the corpus a "knowledge vault" are left as they are so their pass caches stay valid; only user-facing wording now says "library"
The notes-writer code package keeps the name vault, and docs written before the rename keep the old paths as history
evidence: The migration rewrites 1,549 rows across 14 columns on the server, and was trialled on a copy before deploying

you.text: the vault should instead be called library or something better as I do not want it being confused with obsidian's vault
data/, and do not worry at all about any running MCP sessions
you.source: 19 Oct 2026, choosing between library/ and data/

affects: Config defaults and the example config
Code, tests and systemd units
The laptop outbox job that syncs the drop folder
The server deploy, which moves the directory once and rewrites its config
Every stored path in the database, through migration 0037
Running MCP sessions, which need a restart

items.title: The shared Rust crates live in the locus repository
items.question: The crates shared by kairos and keryx (eco-dates) lived in a separate repository, first called eco and then renamed locus-shared, and Slice 1 added the theme to it. The locus window reached it through a relative path that only works with both repositories checked out side by side, and every theme change during the design rounds would otherwise cost a commit and a push there plus a pin bump here.
items.chose: One Rust workspace at the root of this repository holding eco-dates, locus-theme, locus-contract and locus-tui, which replaces the TUI's own folder. kairos and keryx keep their current pins and move their dependency to this repository when each is next touched.
items.why: With the crates here, a theme or contract change during the design rounds is one commit. The plan already merges the repositories once the shared root has real contents, and it now holds the taxonomy, the screen contracts and the theme, so this is the first piece of that merge. kairos and keryx do not break: their pins still resolve because the old GitHub repository is archived rather than deleted and redirects from eco, and Cargo finds a crate by name anywhere in a repository. Moving kairos and keryx themselves into this repository stays a later decision.
over: Keep the name eco: it did not say what the crates are, so it became locus-shared before being folded in
A separate locus-shared repository reached by a relative path: it only builds on a machine with both repositories checked out side by side
A separate locus-shared repository reached by a git pin: every theme change in a design round becomes a commit there, a push, and a pin bump here
A git submodule: two commits per change and a pin that is easy to forget, so a checkout can build old code while looking current
assumes: kairos and keryx need shared-crate changes on roughly the same cadence as locus
The repository's Python side does not get in the way of their builds; if either fails, the shared crates move back out into a repository that holds only them
costs: kairos and keryx builds fetch this whole repository for two small crates
A change here to a crate kairos or keryx uses does not reach them until their pin is bumped, as before
evidence: eco-dates was copied verbatim, identical to locus-shared main at d2191b2; locus-theme came from its theme branch at b74d7a0
This repository is 4.3 MB of history, against kairos's own 10 MB
The old pins still resolve: the GitHub repository is archived, not deleted, and redirects from eco

you.text: why are we calling it eco? ... should it not be called something more accurate to what it is
you.source: 19 Oct 2026, which renamed eco to locus-shared

you.text: fold the shared crates into the repo now
you.source: 19 Oct 2026, offered its own repo, a submodule, or folding in

affects: The locus window and its fixtures, now under crates/
The screen contracts and the theme, edited in one commit each during design rounds
kairos and keryx, which repoint their dependency here when next touched

items.title: The drop folder is organised by area
items.question: The laptop drop folder is the hand path into the library, synced to the server's incoming folder every minute. It had five subfolders (papers, coursework, projects, career, notes) because ingest takes the first folder as the document's category, which mixed what kind of file it is with what it is for, while the plan labels everything by area and does not list a hand drop among the ways sources arrive.
items.chose: Keep the drop folder for files that reach no other path, organised by area like the notes repository and the tablet: studies/<course>/, projects/<name>/, careers/<company or general>/, personal/, with the root meaning let the system decide. Nothing dropped into an area folder counts as his writing, and repository drops are retired.
items.why: Some files still reach no other path: a downloaded PDF, lecture material before the Canvas pull, a career document. A flat folder was chosen first on the understanding that the system labels arrivals, but labelling on arrival is a later slice, so a flat drop would be filed uncategorized. Area folders say what a file is for in the same tree used everywhere else, and the course or project folder survives in the stored incoming path for the later labeller to read. Treating area drops as sources rather than his writing closes a hole where a third-party document dropped in personal or careers would have had positions drawn from it and attributed to him; his own writing arrives through the notes repository and the tablet, recognised by location.
over: The old five subfolders by type (papers, coursework, projects, career, notes): they mixed what kind of file it is, readable from the file, with what it is for, which is not
One flat folder where the system labels what arrives: chosen first and revised the same day, because the system cannot label yet and everything would be filed uncategorized
Dropping the hand path, since the plan's list of ways in does not include it: kept, because some files reach no other path
Keeping repository drops, where a directory under projects was ingested whole as a code snapshot: retired, and the plan removes repository ingest anyway
assumes: The labeller is not yet reliable enough to make the folders unnecessary; once it is, they can go, since the root already works
The library still keys behaviour on the old categories, so each area folder maps onto one; if those categories are retired, the folders map to areas directly
costs: A write-up of his dropped in projects/ counts as a source, not his writing, including the two OQTS specs already filed under the old projects folder; their stored beliefs and links stay, but nothing new is drawn from them
Subfolders are optional, so a root drop stays uncategorized until the labeller exists
The outbox script still lives outside the repository until transcripts sync in Slice 0
evidence: Before this, a text file whose category was note, project or career counted as his, so a third-party .docx in personal or careers would have been attributed to him

you.text: keep it then, but we no longer need the sub-folders, as the system does that for us

you.source: 19 Oct 2026, told the system cannot label yet
19 Oct 2026, on drops in projects/ counting as sources

affects: Ingest's category mapping from area folders, with personal getting its own category
The check for what counts as his writing, in both the structure proposer and the shared owner-authored query
The laptop outbox job and the server's incoming folder
The arrival labeller in a later slice, which reads the course or project folder from the stored path

items.title: How the build is run
items.question: His key work is the planning and guidance, so the method for executing the plan had to be chosen: whether to drive slices with /goal, with chat messages like "start slice 0", or something else in Claude Code.
items.chose: Each slice starts with a spec in docs/redesign/slices/ that he approves before anything is built; one named session per slice, with mechanical steps under /goal with a printed check and a turn bound, judgement stopping to ask, and design work in plain chat; each slice ends with a report in its spec file.
items.why: It puts his time on specs and reports rather than on supervising mechanical work. /goal keeps a session working until a small model judges the condition met, but that judge runs no commands and reads no files, so a condition must name a check whose output is printed, plus a turn bound. Plain chat keeps him in every step, which suits design work at the screen but drifts and loses context over a long slice. The spec lists his decisions up front and flags departures from the plan, and the report gives done, evidence per "done when", deviations and decisions, with big ones going to the tablet.
over: Plain chat messages for every step: keeps him in every step but drifts and loses context over a long slice; kept only for design work
Plan mode: blocks edits until a written plan is approved; the record gives no further reason
Workflows that fan out many agents: suited to wide jobs, not ordered slices
assumes: /goal runs do not often drift from the spec or stop early
He does not find specs a chore he skims; if either fails, steps become smaller and chat-driven, or specs shorter
costs: A spec costs time before each slice; small slices may get a short one
/goal is session-scoped and runs unattended only in auto mode
evidence: The options were checked against Claude Code's docs on 19 Oct 2026, including that the /goal judge sees only what the transcript shows

you.text: the key part of my work is the planning and guidance for the system, I want to make sure we use the best method for executing the plan (ie slash goal or just chat messages to 'start slice 0' etc...)

affects: Every slice of the redesign, starting with Slice 0
The spec files in docs/redesign/slices/
Slice 1, the design work, done in chat with him at the screen

items.title: The plan lives in the repository
items.question: The plan was written and marked up on paper over four versions, but its LaTeX source lived in a session scratchpad that was deleted mid-way, and version 2 had to be recovered from the session transcript. Sessions that build locus need the plan without someone pasting it in, and the existing CLAUDE.md described only the current engine.
items.chose: plan.tex (version 4, final) and info.tex in docs/redesign/ are the source of truth for the redesign, read as source. CLAUDE.md gains a new first section on top saying what is changing, where the plan is, how the build runs and which engine sections are being removed.
items.why: Keeping the plan in the repository means any session sees the redesign first and the engine detail second, and nothing depends on a scratchpad surviving. The existing CLAUDE.md is 706 lines about the engine, much of it hard-won invariants (the silent-failure class, VRAM choreography, idempotent ingest) that stay true for the library. So its sections are kept intact and shrink as their code is removed slice by slice, rather than being rewritten up front.
over: Keeping the plan's source outside the repository, in a session scratchpad: it was deleted mid-way and version 2 had to be recovered from a transcript
Rewriting CLAUDE.md in full up front: much of it is hard-won invariants that stay true for the library, so it shrinks slice by slice instead
assumes: Sessions do not keep acting on engine sections marked for removal
The plan and CLAUDE.md do not drift apart; if either happens, CLAUDE.md is rewritten in full
costs: Two documents for a while, the plan and the engine sections of CLAUDE.md, with a table saying which engine sections are on their way out
evidence: The scratchpad holding the plan's source was deleted mid-way through the four versions, and version 2 was recovered from the session transcript

you.source: 19 Oct 2026, to putting the plan into the repository, orienting CLAUDE.md to the redesign, and writing the Slice 0 spec

The Slice 0 spec, written alongside
Every later decision, which starts where the plan stops
